To include hidden options, change the candidate list built in unknownOption. (Candidate filtering details are a guess.)

Mostly guess (doc mentions optional values and negative-number handling but no specifics). ['--cheese','--verbose'] -> opts {cheese:true, verbose:true}, args []. npm test runs 'node --test && npm run check:type:ts' — Node's built-in test runner (node:test, with node:assert) over tests/, then TypeScript type checks (tsd on typings/index.test-d.ts and tsc). Doc saw 1373 tests, 1372 pass, 1 skipped. Also run npm run check (type, eslint, prettier --check) before a PR.

tests/ directory, one file per feature named tests/<class>.<feature>.test.js. One file: node --test tests/options.choices.test.js. One case: node --test --test-name-pattern="not in choices" tests/options.choices.test.js. Tests use createTestCommand() from tests/testHelpers.js which calls .exitOverride() (so _exit throws CommanderError instead of process.exit) and .configureOutput({writeOut: ()=>{}, writeErr: ()=>{}}) to silence output.

Env is applied after CLI parsing so that parseArg is not called on both the CLI and env values (comment at lib/command.js:1564) — CLI has priority, and if env were applied first a custom parseArg (e.g. accumulator using previous value) would process both. _parseOptionsEnv checks the value source so an env var only overwrites a value whose source is 'default', 'config' or 'env' (or undefined), never 'cli' (lib/command.js:1983) — CLI wins over env, env wins over defaults.
